import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Set up the figure with multiple subplots for comprehensive visualization
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 12))
fig.suptitle('Digital Camera Market Analysis: 1000 Cameras Overview', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)

# Color palette
palette = sns.color_palette("husl", n_colors=len(df['sensor_type'].unique()))

# Plot 1: Price vs Megapixels by Sensor Type
ax1 = axes[0, 0]
for i, sensor in enumerate(df['sensor_type'].unique()):
    subset = df[df['sensor_type'] == sensor]
    ax1.scatter(subset['megapixels'], subset['price_usd'], 
                alpha=0.6, label=sensor, s=30, color=palette[i])
ax1.set_xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_title('Price vs Megapixels by Sensor Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax1.legend(title='Sensor Type', loc='upper left', fontsize=8)
ax1.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# Plot 2: Average Price by Brand (Top 10 brands by count)
ax2 = axes[0, 1]
brand_stats = df.groupby('brand').agg({'price_usd': 'mean', 'brand': 'count'}).rename(columns={'brand': 'count'})
brand_stats = brand_stats.nlargest(10, 'count')
colors = sns.color_palette("viridis", n_colors=10)
bars = ax2.barh(brand_stats.index, brand_stats['price_usd'], color=colors)
ax2.set_xlabel('Average Price (USD)', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_ylabel('Brand', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_title('Average Price by Top 10 Camera Brands', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax2.grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='x')
for bar, price in zip(bars, brand_stats['price_usd']):
    ax2.text(price + 50, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height()/2, f'${price:.0f}', 
             va='center', fontsize=9)

# Plot 3: Camera Distribution by Body Type and 4K Video Capability
ax3 = axes[1, 0]
body_4k = df.groupby(['body_type', 'has_video_4k']).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
body_4k.columns = ['No 4K', 'Has 4K']
body_4k.plot(kind='bar', ax=ax3, color=['#FF6B6B', '#4ECDC4'], edgecolor='black', linewidth=0.5)
ax3.set_xlabel('Body Type', fontsize=11)
ax3.set_ylabel('Number of Cameras', fontsize=11)
ax3.set_title('Camera Count by Body Type & 4K Video Capability', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax3.legend(title='4K Video', fontsize=9)
ax3.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
ax3.grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='y')

# Plot 4: Megapixels Evolution Over Model Years
ax4 = axes[1, 1]
yearly_mp = df.groupby('model_year')['megapixels'].agg(['mean', 'std']).reset_index()
ax4.fill_between(yearly_mp['model_year'], 
                  yearly_mp['mean'] - yearly_mp['std'], 
                  yearly_mp['mean'] + yearly_mp['std'], 
                  alpha=0.3, color='steelblue', label='±1 Std Dev')
ax4.plot(yearly_mp['model_year'], yearly_mp['mean'], 
         color='steelblue', linewidth=2.5, marker='o', markersize=6, label='Mean MP')
ax4.set_xlabel('Model Year', fontsize=11)
ax4.set_ylabel('Megapixels', fontsize=11)
ax4.set_title('Evolution of Camera Resolution Over Time', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax4.legend(fontsize=9)
ax4.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# Adjust layout
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
